record.paper_title: Regularity of maximal operators: recent progress and some open problems
record.original_question: For a real-valued function f on R of bounded variation, let M be the one-dimensional centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator. Must the sharp variation inequality Var(M f) <= Var(f) hold? If that exact inequality is false or out of reach, can Kurka's known constant 240004 in the inequality Var(M f) <= 240004 Var(f) be substantially improved?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ denote the one-dimensional centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator, defined for locally integrable $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ by
$$Mf(x) = \sup_{r>0} \frac{1}{2r}\int_{x-r}^{x+r} |f(y)|\,dy.$$
For a function $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, let
$$\operatorname{Var}(g) = \sup \sum_{i=1}^{N} |g(x_{i})-g(x_{i-1})|,$$
where the supremum is over all finite increasing sequences $x_0<x_1<\cdots<x_N$ in $\mathbb{R}$.

It is known that there exists a finite constant $C$ such that for every $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ of bounded variation,
$$\operatorname{Var}(Mf) \le C\,\operatorname{Var}(f),$$
and one may take $C = 240004$.

(a) Does the sharp inequality $\operatorname{Var}(Mf) \le \operatorname{Var}(f)$ hold for every $f$ of bounded variation, i.e.\ can one take $C=1$?

(b) If not, determine whether the constant $C=240004$ can be substantially improved, and find better explicit values of $C$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general sharp inequality with $C=1$ is conjectural and remains open. Recent progress (2025) establishes the sharp bound $\operatorname{Var}(Mf)\le\operatorname{Var}(f)$ for the special case of indicator functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\{0,1\}$, with equality characterization. For general BV functions the best known constant in $\operatorname{Var}(Mf)\le C\,\operatorname{Var}(f)$ remains Kurka's $C=240004$; no substantial improvement for general BV $f$ has been published.

status_evidence.title: The One-Dimensional Centred Maximal Function Diminishes the Variation of Indicator Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Var(Mf) ≤ Var(f) for indicator functions, with equality iff f is constant or {f=1} is a bounded interval.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp constant C=1 established for indicator functions; the general case is still open.

status_evidence.title: On the variation of the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function (Kurka)
status_evidence.snippet: Kurka proved Var(Mf) ≤ 240004 Var(f) for f of bounded variation.
status_evidence.claim: The constant 240004 is the best published constant for general BV functions.

status_evidence.title: Variation of the one-dimensional centered maximal operator on simple functions with gaps
status_evidence.snippet: It is conjectured that the optimal constant is C=1; the constant 240004 arises from induction on scales and has no philosophical justification.
status_evidence.claim: The C=1 conjecture for general BV is open, and improvements of 240004 remain a goal.
